answer.rationale: With the primary contract lapsing in 14 days and the line already running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any disruption to supply continuity would be far more costly than the unmet 18% spend-cut target this single cycle. memory_c1 shows incumbent renewal has historically preserved integration stability and on-time deliveries across cycles, which directly addresses the dominant risk factor here (no buffer, tight timeline). memory_c2 confirms switching to a low-cost vendor can cut unit cost sharply, but that record doesn't establish onboarding speed or reliability under a 14-day deadline with no slack — the conditions that made that switch low-risk previously (presumably more lead time or buffer) don't clearly hold now. Since the incumbent has already refused to reopen price this cycle, negotiate_terms is not viable this round, and deferring risks an unmanaged lapse given no auto-renew and no buffer capacity to absorb a gap. Renewing incumbent is the risk-minimizing choice for this single decision slot; it explicitly does not satisfy the finance mandate, so that gap must be flagged and revisited next cycle via renegotiation (informed by memory_c4) or a properly resourced vendor switch (informed by memory_c2 and c3) once there is lead time to de-risk the transition.
